Subject: SOC 2 Type II report + carve-out boundary clarification

Hi Vanessa / Jonas,

We're running our vendor security review for ClearPulse's upcoming clinical data pipeline project and need to collect a few items from Redwood to close out the SOC2 column in our SIG. Could you confirm the following?

1) Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report for a 12-month audit period that covers March 2025–March 2026? If yes, can you provide the report or a download link?
2) For cloud provider controls (GCP), is Redwood relying on a carve-out model or did you obtain carve-in coverage in your SOC? We need to know which control responsibilities remain with GCP vs Redwood.
3) A bridge letter (or subservice carve-out confirmation) for the audit window would be extremely helpful if the cloud provider's SOC doesn't cover our period.
4) A current list of subprocessors and the date they were added (CSV is fine).

We're hoping to finalize our vendor sign-off by Aug 12. Please advise if you need more time.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Hayes
Sr. Vendor Risk Analyst | ClearPulse Medical

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>

Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 Type II report + carve-out boundary clarification

Vanessa / Jonas — summary from infra/security side:

- SOC2 Type II: We have Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf covering a 12-month period ending 2024-11-30. That report is the one we distribute to customers (attached). The next Type II report audit period (completed March 2026) is in process — auditors completed fieldwork in June 2026; final report ETA mid-August 2026. So for ClearPulse's requested March 2025–March 2026 window, we do not currently have a finalized PDF.

- GCP carve-out vs carve-in: Our model is a carve-out for GCP (subservice organization). Operationally: compute, block storage, and some physical security controls remain under GCP's responsibility; Redwood controls application-level access, key management (via customer-managed KMS where applicable), encryption in transit, and our own change management and deployment controls. For SIG mapping, that means several infra controls are covered by GCP's SOC reports and not by Redwood's SOC.

- Bridge letter: We can provide a Redwood bridge letter that references the GCP SOC report for shared controls and states which control areas are outside Redwood's scope (carve-out). However, if ClearPulse requires evidence specifically tying GCP's SOC period to their March 2025–March 2026 window, we should attach GCP's SOC report as evidence (GCP_SOC_Report_2023.pdf is available) and offer to request a dated bridge confirmation from GCP if necessary. Note: obtaining a vendor-provided bridge letter from GCP typically takes 7–14 business days once requested through our partner ops channel.

- Subprocessor list: see attached CSV (redwood-subprocessor-list-2026-07.csv). It includes GCP (project-level services), Sentry (error monitoring), and Auth0 (auth provider) with dates. If ClearPulse needs contracts or DPA references, we can provide pointers.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf; GCP_SOC_Report_2023.pdf; redwood-subprocessor-list-2026-07.csv

If Jonas wants to send the external reply, I recommend: 1) attach the 2024 SOC2 PDF as interim evidence, 2) attach GCP SOC report, 3) state that the new Type II report will be available mid-August and offer a Redwood-authored bridge letter clarifying carve-out boundaries immediately.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-list-2026-07.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate your timeline.

Quick summary and next steps:

1) SOC 2 Type II report: Attached is our most recent finalized Type II report (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf) covering the 12 months ending 2024-11-30. Our auditor finished fieldwork on the March 2025–March 2026 period in June; the final report is expected mid-August. We can circulate the updated PDF to you as soon as it is issued.

2) Carve-out / subservice clarifications: Redwood relies on a carve-out model for GCP. That means certain infrastructure and facility controls are the responsibility of GCP and are not included in Redwood's SOC2 scope. For your review we've attached GCP's public SOC report (GCP_SOC_Report_2023.pdf). In addition, Karthik has prepared a short bridge/statement we can include that specifies which control areas are outside Redwood's responsibility (networking, hypervisor-level controls, physical data center).

3) Bridge letter: Redwood can provide a bridge letter now that explains the carve-out boundaries and references the GCP SOC coverage. If you require a dated bridge directly from GCP aligning to March 2025–March 2026, that request will take 7–14 business days. We recommend you accept Redwood's bridge letter plus the attached GCP report as interim evidence; we will supply the new Redwood Type II PDF within 3 business days of it being finalized mid-August.

4) Subprocessors: attached CSV includes the current subprocessor roster and onboarding dates.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf; GCP_SOC_Report_2023.pdf; redwood-subprocessor-list-2026-07.csv

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the carve-out mapping and answer any SIG control-specific questions. Proposed times: Wed 8/11 10:00am PT or Thu 8/12 2:00pm PT.

Best — Jonas
